title: Midlane capacity burn and price elasticity notebook
content:
Summary:
This notebook models a midlane (medium-growth) scenario for Q4 2025–Q4 2026 focusing on: 1) headcount ramp timing and cash flow impact, 2) GPU procurement cadence (reserved vs spot), and 3) a price-elasticity sensitivity matrix that ties per-token price changes to revenue, margin, and hiring triggers.

Key outcomes (short):
- Base plan (midlane) requires +18 FTEs across Eng/Infra/Customer Success over 12 months; peak incremental monthly burn hits $1.12M in Jul 2026.
- Moving 30% of GPU procurement to spot reduces monthly infra cash burn by ~$120k but increases variance; requires 2 additional SRE headcount for ops mitigation.
- A -10% price step (per-token) short-term increases consumption but reduces near-term gross margin by ~3.8 p.p.; if sustained, triggers hiring freeze at -12% revenue delta threshold.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Base ARR baseline used: $42.4M (run-rate at 2025-10).
- Token mix: 70% generation (text), 25% embeddings, 5% rerankers.
- Average tokens per-API call: generation 1,850; embeddings 750; rerankers 4,200.
- Unit economics: compute cost per 1k gen tokens (on reserved GPU baseline) = $0.024; embeddings = $0.012 per 1k; rerankers = $0.035 per 1k.
- Sales/COGS/G&A allocations by FTE: eng $210k fully loaded, infra/SRE $240k, customer success $150k, product $190k, finance/ops $170k.
- Procurement mix baseline: 80% reserved GPUs, 20% spot.
- Hiring lead time: 8 weeks for engineers, 4 weeks for CS/ops.

Sheet A -- Headcount plan (monthly snapshot, FY26-Q2 to FY26-Q4):
Columns: Month, New Hires (Eng), New Hires (Infra/SRE), New Hires (CS), Net HC Delta, Incremental Monthly Payroll ($k), Cumulative Payroll ($k)

Notes: payroll numbers include ramped prorated salaries + benefits + recruiting fees amortized. July spike reflects vendor-contracted hires onboarding and finalizing dedicated capacity commitment.

Sheet B -- GPU capacity burn schedule (hours & $k per month):
Columns: Month, Reserved GPU hrs, Spot GPU hrs, Reserved $k, Spot $k, Total infra $k
Sample rows:

Notes: reserved $k assumes multi-month commitment amortized; spot $k highly variable (we assume average spot price 40% of on-demand but with 2x variance).

Sheet C -- Pricing sensitivity matrix (per 1k tokens on generation route):
Scenarios modeled: -15%, -10%, -5%, Base, +5%, +10% price steps. For each: change in unit price, expected % change in volume (elasticity assumptions), revenue delta (12-monthized), gross margin delta (p.p.), and hires trigger flag.
Elasticity assumptions (endogenous):
- Short term (0–3m): elasticity = -0.6 (small consumption uptick for price down).
- Medium term (3–12m): elasticity = -1.1 for price decreases >5% (customers optimize/pivot).
- Enterprise sticky cohort elasticity: -0.2 (less sensitive).

Matrix (high-level numbers):
-15% price: unit price -> -15%; volume change immediate +9%; 12m revenue delta = -7.2% (~-$3.05M); gross margin -7.8 p.p.; hiring trigger: HIRING_FREEZE if revenue < -10%
-10% price: volume +6%; 12m revenue delta = -3.8% (~-$1.62M); gross margin -3.8 p.p.; hiring trigger: hiring slowdown recommended if sustained >3 months
-5% price: volume +3%; 12m revenue delta = -1.6% (~-$0.68M); gross margin -1.6 p.p.; hiring trigger: monitor
Base price: baseline
+5% price: volume -2%; 12m revenue delta = +2.8% (~+$1.18M); gross margin +1.9 p.p.; hiring trigger: greenlight +2 hires if sustained 6 months
+10% price: volume -4%; 12m revenue delta = +6.3% (~+$2.67M); gross margin +4.1 p.p.; hiring trigger: accelerate hiring +5 FTEs

Interpretation notes:
- Because compute cost has a large fixed reserved component, small price decreases compress margin disproportionately until we absorb more volume onto caching/batching improvements.
- A tactical price step (-10%) timed with a product launch (feature-driven usage growth) could be neutral if medium-term elasticity materializes >1.5x assumed. But the safe cash-first posture requires a plan for hiring throttles if revenue drops >4% sustained.

Stress runs (two quick ones):
1) Conservative stress: price -10% + spot outage (20% reserved fallback premium) => incremental monthly burn +$260k and margin breach -> hiring freeze and deferral of two non-critical infra projects.
2) Aggressive demand: price -5% and product-driven 40% usage growth on generation route -> net revenue +4%, margin flat (because higher cache hit reduces incremental cost), recommend 3 additional Eng hires for optimization and +1 SRE.

Actionable recommendations (finance ops + exec):
- Approve midlane hiring tranche conditional on monthly revenue delta checks (auto-throttle clauses). Hire windows: 60% of planned Eng hires in Q2–Q3 2026, rest in Q4.
- Shift procurement target to 70/30 reserved/spot; maintain a 10% operational buffer (cash reserve) for spot volatility.
- Implement a 6-week price experiment framework: roll -5% in targeted non-enterprise segments for 6 weeks; monitor usage and margin. If 6-week revenue delta >+1%, consider broader roll.
- Prepare a playbook for rapid hiring freeze and project deferral: list of top 6 projects to pause and candidate redeployments.

Appendix snippets (quick tables and KPIs):
KPIs tracked monthly: Net new MRR, Token volume (1k units), Compute $/1k gen tokens, Gross margin p.p., Net cash burn, Hiring velocity (FTEs/month), GPU reserved utilization %.

Open questions / uncertainties (notes to reviewers):
- Spot variance may be correlated with cloud-market events; need a 6-month empirical sample to calibrate variance and ops overhead.
- Elasticity estimates are informed by internal A/Bs and public benchmarks but high-variance for new routes (e.g., multimodal).
- Talent market shifts could move fully loaded costs +/-12% year over year — sensitivity test recommended.

Next steps (owners):
- Finance (Ethan Morales): finalize cash cushion thresholds and incorporate into monthly close (due 2026-02-10).
- Infra procurement (Ava Chen): model 70/30 reserved/spot run with 3 different spot-volatility bands; present on 2026-02-18.
- Headcount (Maya Rodriguez): convert this plan to hiring pipeline in Greenhouse; include backfill timelines by 2026-02-12.

Notes for doc hygiene: this is a working workbook intended for internal review; numbers are directional and assume current contract pricing/benchmarks. Update linked artifacts after A/B results and procurement simulations are available.
